The drafters of this piece were smart, it's not reducing Load-shedding to 6hrs in 24hrs but splitting the 12hrs (of the whole day) into Two segments. This means, in 24hrs, instead of having a continuous 12hr load-shedding, we will be having the 12hrs but split as follows:

A day has 24hrs, meaning there are 4 Six hours(es), hence the first 6hrs you have power, the next 6hrs you have no power, again the next 6hrs you have power and the last 6hrs you don't have power, bringing the total to 12hrs with and 12hrs without power in a 24hrs day.

LOAD SHEDDING, WHAT ARE OUR OPTIONS?

Most of you that follow me on these Socials by now you understand where I stand politically, but allow me to be apolitical as we look at this issue because it is not an issue for the greens, the reds or the blues, it's one issue that is affecting all of us directly.

Personally, I celebrated when the President assured the nation that load shedding was an issue of the past and he was quick to highlight what was done. On two more occasions, the President still affirmed his position.

So really, it is a shock for us to have load shedding now and I want to believe President HH is as shocked as all of us.

This challenge has befallen us as a nation and something has to be done in the interim to save the few jobs that we have around.

1. To begin with, 12 hours of load shedding is too way much. In 24 hours we sleep for 8 hours, we are load shedded for 12 hours, now have 4 hours to work in a day which has now been split into breaks of 2 hours. This alone has killed productivity in so many ways than we can imagine. My proposal is that load shedding must be done equally. There are places where there is no load shedding yet there is no hospital nearby. So if the hours have to reduce, it must be done equally!

2.1 Alternative sources of energy. Looking at the foregoing, the best government can do is to look at fuel pump prices quarterly as opposed to monthly as is the case so that people can be able to forecast longer. If we can't plan properly in business it becomes difficult.

2.2 Solar Energy. In one of my interactions on these Socials, I had a chat with the President of the Solar Industry in Zambia regarding Solar prices and government efforts to make the costs affordable, what came out of this interaction is that solar, much as it is good, is an expensive alternative and not everyone can afford it. Ni mutengo wa mutima, pwapwa naka nondo as a mbashela, how many people can afford that? My proposal is that, the few that have solar energy and are able generate excess energy, let them be allowed to channel that back into the grid, Zesco should pay for that so that we have more. This should also be able to encourage more people and Companies to go the solar way.

3. We need a 24 hour Economy like now. This can be done by repealing the labor act. What this will mean is that if I have a tailoring Business and I have 6 employees, instead of firing half of them in advent of load shedding, I just have to split them into night and day so that whether power is available in the night or day, production still goes on and I won't be sued for going against our labor laws as a business owner. This is very important! Extremely important because the "load" that we need to shed happens mostly between 7am and 5pm because those are our working hours currently but if we can spread the hours, we will literally shed the load, thereby increase productivity and save jobs.

4. Let us change the law on power generation. Let the private sector come in and invest in power generation. Let people with big money make solar farms and sale Electricity to Zesco, let people set up wind equipment for energy generation and sale to Zesco which has the infrastructure to distribute the power.

In concluding, fellow Zambians, allow me to point out that this is a crisis and as such requires our concerted effort if we have to overcome it.

No President will have peaceful sleep knowing what has befallen the nation, let us unite for the common good of our country.

If you think things are expensive now, they will be worse with the coming of load shedding, so we have to work together to save our ailing Economy.
